ROUND 1 supplemental performance verdict: BLOCK.
Subject: pr:330
Head: 1c998e75d005eaa70266314da25a533204ab7f70

This supersedes my PASS-WITH-NOTES at this head (governance commit4dd77fd). New, independent actual-adapter witnesses show normal-shape teardown failures and repeated non-progressing launch bursts. The earlier32-pane happy-path CI does not clear these cases. This remains round1; the findings are within the original batch-size/failure-isolation scope.

Blocking evidence:
1. Large-batch transport failure: a300-entry minimum-width command packet was rejected as "command too long". The actual adapter made34 launches in2.053271291s, returned failure, and left the live pipe, marker and sink intact. The fixture repeats one owned pane to avoid creating300 processes. It is not a300-live-pane benchmark; applicability to300 distinct panes is an inference from the unchanged per-entry command encoding: distinct pane IDs cannot make this minimum-width packet smaller. A realistic larger fleet therefore cannot rely on the advertised single batch completing.
2. Retained-exited pane starves a live suffix: with an exited pane still retained/listed in the middle, the actual adapter made46 launches in2.048724458s. The first tap completed, but the later live tap remained pipe1 with its marker and sink. The command list repeatedly failed at "target pane has exited". This violates the batch port's failure-isolation promise: one pane's failure must not keep another's tap attached. The previous per-pane detach loop could continue to the unrelated live pane after one error.

Root cause and cost:
- The batch is neither transport-size bounded nor split before execution. A permanent packet rejection leaves every pending entry unchanged.
- A retained exited pane remains in pending because its marker exists. Retrying the same ordered list keeps failing at that same pane before reaching the suffix.
- The25ms retry loop treats both conditions as convergence races until its2s grace. Thus the healthy1-launch claim becomes34/46 failed or partially progressing launches, and teardown still fails. The observations are private-fixture counts/times, not measured whole-fleet rates.
- This is more than optional hardening: valid large-batch shape and ordinary retained-exited pane state produce a wrong teardown result plus repeat-launch cost. Keep the ownership brakes; bound command packets and isolate terminal/permanent per-pane failures so unrelated owned taps can complete. A concrete fix belongs to the coder, not this read-only review.
